# Volume 1 — CHAPTER II. Obed Abernethy Is Surprised

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Riding the sorrel mare, OBED Abernethy traveled at an easy pace across the eight miles that led to Alder River. Along its pleasant stretch, the road passed between cozy farmsteads, occasionally penetrating a patch of fragrant fir forest or descending into a dip where the delicate blossoms of wild plum trees dangled. A sweet fragrance from numerous apple orchards filled the air, and far off, the meadows inclined toward the horizon's hazy shades of purple and pearl; while
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0000 }

“The small birds warbled as though this was The single summer day of the entire year.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0001 }

In his own way, Obed found pleasure in the journey, save for those instances when he encountered women and was required to bow his head to them—because on St. Brendan’s Island custom dictates that you bow your head to everyone you pass along the way, regardless of whether they are known to you or not.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0002 }

Obed feared every woman with the exception of Thirza and Mrs. Agatha; a uneasy sensation possessed him that those enigmatic beings were quietly mocking him. In believing this, he could well have been correct, since he was an unusual-appearing individual, possessing an awkward frame alongside lengthy iron-gray hair reaching his hunching shoulders, as well as a thick, gentle brown beard that had been on his face continually from the age of twenty. Indeed, his appearance at twenty closely resembled his appearance at sixty, possessing merely somewhat less gray.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0003 }

Upon getting to Alder River, he saw no trace of a train; believing he had arrived prematurely, he secured his horse in the yard belonging to the modest Alder River hotel and crossed to the station house. Hardly anyone was on the long platform, where the sole living being visible was a girl seated on a stack of shingles at the very far end. Barely registering her gender, Obed edged past her as fast as he could while avoiding her gaze. If he had observed her, he could scarcely have missed the strained stiffness and anticipation in her posture and face. She was perched there anticipating something or someone, and because sitting and waiting was the sole option available at that moment, she sat and waited with every ounce of her strength and devotion.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0004 }

Obed met the stationmaster as he was securing the ticket office before leaving to have supper at home, and inquired whether the five-thirty train would arrive shortly.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0005 }

“The train due at five-thirty arrived and departed thirty minutes since,” replied that lively employee. “However, one rider was left behind for you—a young girl. She is seated on the shingles outdoors. I requested that she enter the ladies’ waiting room, yet she told me solemnly that she chose to remain outdoors. ‘There was more scope for imagination,’ she stated. She’s a character, I’d tell you.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0006 }

“A girl is not what I’m expecting,” Obed stated blankly. “A boy is who I’ve come for. Here is where he should be. For me, Mrs. Alexander Tranter was supposed to bring him over from Nova Scotia.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0007 }

A whistle was blown by the stationmaster.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0008 }

“There appears to be an error,” he remarked. “Mrs. Tranter exited the train alongside that girl and entrusted her to me. She stated that you and your sister were taking her in from an orphan asylum and that you would arrive to collect her shortly. That comprises my entire knowledge of the matter—and I possess no additional orphans hidden around here.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0009 }

“I do not comprehend,” Obed uttered powerlessly, desiring Thirza’s presence to manage the circumstance.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0010 }

“Well, you ought to interrogate the girl,” the stationmaster remarked indifferently. “I expect she can give an explanation—she certainly possesses a tongue in her head. Perhaps they lacked any boys belonging to the type you requested.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0011 }

Because he was famished, he strolled off in a cheerful manner, leaving the unlucky Obed to face a task he found more daunting than confronting a lion in its lair—approaching a girl—an unfamiliar girl—a parentless girl—and asking her to explain why she was not a male. Feeling deep internal distress, Obed pivoted and moved at a slow, dragging pace along the platform in her direction.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0012 }

Her gaze had been fixed on him from the moment he walked past her, and she kept her eyes on him still. Obed was not glancing in her direction, nor would he have discerned her true appearance had he done so, yet a typical onlooker would have noticed the following: A girl roughly eleven years old, dressed in a wincey frock of yellowish-gray that was exceedingly brief, snug, and unattractive. On her head was a washed-out brown sailor hat, and underneath it, stretching down her back, hung two plaitings of exceptionally dense, unmistakably red hair. Small, pale, and slender was her face, which was additionally covered in freckles; her mouth was wide, as were her eyes, which appeared green under certain lights and tempers and gray under others.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0013 }

Up to this point, such was the view of a typical spectator; yet a remarkable spectator could have noticed that her chin was exceptionally sharp and distinct; that her large eyes overflowed with energy and life; that her mouth possessed sweet lips and rich expression; that her brow was expansive and prominent; to sum up, our perceptive remarkable spectator might have determined that an unexceptional spirit did not dwell within the frame of this wandering female child whom bashful Obed Abernethy feared in such a laughable manner.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0014 }

Because she realized he was approaching her, she stood up immediately, which saved Obed from having to talk first; one of her slim, tan hands gripped the handle of a worn, outmoded carpet-bag, while she offered him the other.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0015 }

“You are Mr. Obed Abernethy of Grey Shutters, I assume?” she inquired, her voice sounding distinctly pure and pleasant. “Seeing you makes me very happy. The fear that you were not arriving for me was starting to take hold, and I was picturing every possible occurrence that could have stopped you. My decision was finalized that had you failed to collect me this evening, I would walk down the path toward that large wild cherry-tree located at the turn, and scale it so I could spend the entire night inside. Fear would not touch me at all, and resting inside a wild cherry-tree completely covered in white blossoms under the moonlight would be wonderful, wouldn't it? One could picture living within marble halls, couldn't one? Furthermore, I felt entirely certain that you would arrive to get me when morning came, had you missed this evening.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0016 }

Clumsily, Obed held the thin, small hand within his own; right then, his course of action became clear to him. It was impossible for him to inform this girl, whose eyes shone, that an error had occurred; instead, he planned to bring her to his residence and allow Thirza to break the news. Regardless of any mix-up, she was unable to remain at Alder River in any case, meaning every query and clarification could be put off until he arrived securely at Grey Shutters.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0017 }

“I regret that I arrived late,” he uttered timidly. “Follow me. Over in the yard is where the horse is waiting. Let me take your bag.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0018 }

“Oh, I am able to hold it,” the youngster answered brightly. “Its weight is light. All my earthly possessions are inside, yet it isn't heavy. Furthermore, unless it is held in a precise manner the handle detaches—therefore I should hold onto it since I possess the specific trick to it. This carpet-bag is remarkably ancient. Oh, my heart is filled with joy that you arrived, although resting inside a wild cherry-tree would have been lovely too. Our carriage ride is quite lengthy, isn't it? Eight miles was the distance Mrs. Tranter mentioned. This makes me happy since taking rides in carriages brings me delight. Oh, residing with you and being yours feels utterly marvelous to me. Belonging to anyone has never happened to me—not in truth. However, existing in the asylum was the most terrible thing. My stay there lasted merely four months, yet that proved sufficient. You likely have no experience being an orphan inside an asylum, which means comprehending the feeling is impossible for you. What it is like surpasses the worst things you could envision. Expressing such thoughts was sinful of me according to Mrs. Tranter, yet committing a sin was not my intention. Committing a sin without realizing it happens with great ease, doesn't it? The folk running the asylum were kind, you see. Nonetheless, an asylum offers very little room for imagining—except concerning the remaining orphans. Inventing stories about them proved rather fascinating—such as conceiving that the girl residing on the adjacent seat was truly the offspring of a belted earl, stolen from her mother and father during babyhood by a heartless nanny who perished prior to confessing. Nights were spent lying awake creating those fantasies, owing to my lack of daytime hours for it. That likely accounts for my extreme thinness—I am terribly skinny, am I not? My bones possess not a scrap of flesh. Conceiving myself as lovely and chubby, displaying dimples on my elbows, is something I truly adore.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0019 }

At this point Obed’s associate ceased speaking, driven to silence in part by her breathlessness and in part by their arrival at the vehicle. She uttered nothing further until after their departure from the settlement, as they were traveling down a brief, sharp decline along a section of path excavated so profoundly into the tender earth that the mounds, bordered by flowering wild cherry-trees and slender white birches, rose multiple feet overhead.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0020 }

Reaching out her hand, the young girl snapped off a wild plum branch that grazed against the buggy's side.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0021 }

“Is that not lovely? That tree stretching from the shore, completely pale and delicate—what did it remind you of?” she inquired.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0022 }

“Well now, I don’t know,” Obed remarked.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0023 }

“Naturally, a bride—a bride entirely in white accompanied by a beautiful, misty veil. Although I have not actually witnessed one, I can picture her appearance in my mind. I do not anticipate becoming a bride myself at any point. Because I am so plain, no man will ever wish to take me as his wife—except perhaps a foreign missionary. It seems to me that a foreign missionary might not be overly picky. Nevertheless, I genuinely pray to own a white dress at some time in the future. That represents the ultimate peak of my earthly happiness. Pretty garments are things I simply adore. Furthermore, to the best of my memory, I have not owned a single pretty dress in my entire existence—yet that naturally leaves even more to anticipate in the future, doesn't it? Besides, I am able to picture myself clad in magnificent attire. On this very morning as I departed the asylum, wearing this dreadful old wincey garment made me feel utterly mortified. As you are aware, every single orphan was required to wear them. During the previous winter, a storekeeper located in Marden gifted three hundred yards of wincey to the orphanage. Certain individuals claimed his action stemmed from an inability to sell the fabric, yet I prefer to think it arose from pure benevolence, wouldn't you agree? After boarding the train, I was consumed by the sensation that every single person was staring at me with pity. However, I immediately set to work picturing myself wearing an exquisite gown of light blue silk—for if one engages in imagination, one ought to picture something truly grand—alongside a large hat covered in blossoms and swaying feathers, accompanied by a gold watch, kid leather gloves, and boots. My spirits rose instantly, allowing me to relish my journey to the Island to the absolute maximum. Boarding and traveling on the vessel did not make me the least bit ill. Mrs. Tranter was spared from illness as well, even though she usually experiences it. She remarked that she lacked the time to become sick, being fully occupied with ensuring I refrained from tumbling into the water. She declared she had never encountered anyone quite like me for wandering around. Still, if my wandering prevented her from suffering seasickness, it proved to be a fortunate thing, didn't it? On top of that, I wished to observe every single sight available on that vessel, since I had no idea if I would ever receive a second chance. Oh, look, there are many additional cherry trees entirely covered in blossoms! A place more filled with blooms than this Island could not exist. Already I adore it completely, and the prospect of residing here fills me with joy. I had frequently been told that St. Brendan’s Island surpassed every other location on earth in beauty, and I used to picture myself residing here, though I never truly anticipated that I would. It brings such joy when the things you picture become reality, doesn't it? Even so, those crimson roads appear extraordinarily peculiar. Upon boarding the train at Port Marlow, as those crimson roads started streaming past, I inquired of Mrs. Tranter regarding the cause of their red color, to which she replied that she was ignorant of the reason and begged me for mercy's sake to stop peppering her with queries. She mentioned that I must have presented her with a thousand queries already. I imagine I truly had done so, but in what manner can a person learn about the world if they refrain from asking questions? Besides, what actually causes the roads to be red?”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0024 }

“Well now, I don’t know,” Obed remarked.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0025 }

“Well, discovering that is among the things to be done eventually. Isn’t it wonderful when you consider how many things exist for us to discover? It simply causes me to be happy that I am living—this world possesses so much interest. If we were completely knowledgeable about every single thing, it would not be nearly as interesting, right? In that scenario, there would not be any room left for imagination, right? However, am I speaking excessively? Folks constantly inform me that I speak too much. Do you prefer that I remain silent? Should you tell me to, I will cease. I am capable of stopping once I decide to do so, even though it is tough.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0026 }

Far beyond his own expectations, Obed was having a good time. Similar to the majority of taciturn individuals, he appreciated loquacious companions provided they handled the conversation entirely on their own and required no participation from his side. Nevertheless, he had never anticipated deriving pleasure from the company of a young girl. Female adults were already difficult enough in all honesty, yet young girls were even more dreadful. He loathed how they habitually edged by him bashfully, casting askance looks, as though anticipating that he would devour them in one bite should they dare to utter anything. That described the Brierley style of a refined young girl. This freckled enchantress, however, was entirely distinct, and even though his less nimble mind struggled somewhat to match her swift train of thought, he considered that he “kind of liked her chatter.” Consequently, he remarked with his customary bashfulness:
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0027 }

“Oh, you are free to speak as long as you wish. It does not bother me.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0028 }

“Oh, my happiness is so great. My knowledge is certain that you and I will have a fine time getting along with one another. Talking whenever a person desires to, without receiving instructions that the seeing of children is preferred over their hearing, brings such relief. That very thing has been repeated to me fully a million times if it has happened a single time. Furthermore, I am mocked by people for employing large words. Nevertheless, when a person possesses grand ideas, the utilization of grand words becomes necessary to convey them, does it not?”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0029 }

“Well now, that appears sensible,” Obed said.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0030 }

“Mrs. Tranter mentioned that my tongue had to be hinged in the center. However, it is not—it is securely attached at one side. Mrs. Tranter mentioned that your home was called Grey Shutters. I inquired of her regarding everything about it. And she mentioned that trees grew all surrounding it. I felt happier than before. I simply adore trees. And there were none whatsoever surrounding the asylum, except a couple of sad tiny-winy ones in the front area having small white-painted cage-like frames surrounding them. They merely appeared like orphans as well, those trees did. Looking at them used to cause me to desire weeping. I was accustomed to telling them, ‘Oh, you poor little things! If you were located in a very large forest surrounded by other trees and small mosses and June bells spreading across your roots and a stream nearby and birds making music in your limbs, you would be able to expand, would you not? However, you are unable to where you stand. I understand precisely the way you feel, little trees.’ I experienced sadness about abandoning them earlier today. One becomes extremely fond of objects like those, does one not? Does a stream exist anywhere close to Grey Shutters? I omitted asking Mrs. Tranter about that.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0031 }

“Well now, indeed, there is one located directly beneath the house.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0032 }

“Imagine that. Residing by a stream has forever been among my desires. However, I didn’t think it would ever happen. Wishes rarely become reality, isn’t that so? Wouldn’t it be delightful if they were to? Yet at this very moment, I feel almost entirely happy. I am unable to feel completely happy because—well, what shade would you say this is?”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0033 }

She flipped a single long, shiny braid over her slender shoulder, holding it right in front of Obed’s face. Deciding on the shades of women's hair was something Obed was unaccustomed to doing, yet there was little room for uncertainty regarding this particular matter.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0034 }

“Red is what it is, isn’t it?” was his remark.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0035 }

With a sigh that appeared to originate from the bottom of her feet and breathe out every grief of the centuries, the girl permitted her plait to fall back down.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0036 }

“Indeed, it is red,” she uttered in a resigned manner. “Now the reason why I am unable to be completely happy is clear to you. No person with red hair could be. The remaining traits—my skinniness, the freckles, and the green eyes—do not bother me as much. I am able to mentally picture them gone. I am able to imagine possessing a gorgeous rose-leaf skin tone alongside beautiful starry violet eyes. However, that red hair cannot be imagined away by me. I try as hard as I can. My mind thinks, ‘Now a glorious black belongs to my hair, black as the raven’s wing.’ Yet during the entire time, my knowledge is that it is simply red, which causes my heart to break. It shall serve as my lifelong sorrow. Once, within a novel, I read about a girl whose sorrow lasted a lifetime, though red hair was not what it was. Pure gold was her hair, which rippled back from her alabaster brow. What does an alabaster brow mean? Finding out was something I never managed. Are you able to inform me?”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0037 }

“Well now, I’m afraid I can’t,” replied Obed, whose head was starting to spin slightly. His sensation mirrored a moment from his reckless childhood when a friend had persuaded him to ride the carousel during a picnic.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0038 }

“Well, regardless of what it happened to be, it had to be a pleasant thing, given that her beauty was divine. Has the thought ever crossed your mind of how it would feel to possess divine beauty?”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0039 }

“Well then, no, I have not,” admitted Obed with candid simplicity.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0040 }

“I have, frequently. If the option were yours, which would you prefer to be—divinely beautiful, dazzlingly clever, or angelically good?”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0041 }

“Well now, I—I am not entirely sure.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0042 }

“I am unable to as well. Choosing is something I can never do. However, it matters very little in reality, as my becoming either is quite improbable. My ever achieving angelic goodness is an impossibility. According to Mrs. Tranter—oh, Mr. Abernethy! Oh, Mr. Abernethy!! Oh, Mr. Abernethy!!!”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0043 }

Mrs. Tranter had not stated that; furthermore, the child had not fallen from the buggy, nor had Obed performed anything remarkable. They had merely navigated a bend along the road and come upon the “Avenue.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0044 }

The residents of Stonebridge referred to a four- or five-hundred-yard section of roadway as the “Avenue,” a path fully covered by an arch of massive, far-reaching apple trees that had been set in the ground long before by a peculiar elderly farmer. Above, a continuous roof of sweet-smelling, snow-white blossoms stretched out. Beneath the branches, the air was saturated with a violet dusk, while off in the distance, a sight of the colorful evening sky glowed like a massive stained-glass rose window positioned at the far end of a cathedral’s central walkway.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0045 }

The child appeared to be struck speechless by its beauty. Reclining in the buggy, she held her thin hands clasped in front of her, raising her face with ecstasy toward the white magnificence overhead. She neither shifted nor uttered a word, even after they had exited and were traveling down the lengthy incline toward Stonebridge. With an enraptured countenance, she continued to look into the distant, sunlit west, her eyes beholding visions that marched grandly over that radiant backdrop. They traveled on in quietness through Stonebridge, a lively small town where dogs barked in their direction, young boys jeered, and inquisitive faces looked out from the windows. The child remained silent even after another three miles were left behind them. Clearly, she possessed the capacity to maintain quietness just as vigorously as she could speak.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0046 }

“I suppose you must be feeling rather exhausted and famished,” Obed hazarded eventually, explaining her prolonged period of silence using the sole cause that occurred to him. “However, our remaining journey is quite short—just one more mile.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0047 }

Releasing a profound sigh, she emerged from her daydream and directed her eyes toward him, bearing the visionary look of a spirit that had been roaming in distant realms, guided by the stars.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0048 }

“Oh, Mr. Abernethy,” she murmured in a low voice, “the location we passed through—that pale location—what could it have been?”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0049 }

“Well now, the Avenue must be what you mean,” Obed remarked following a couple of seconds of deep thought. “It is a sort of lovely spot.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0050 }

“Pretty? Oh, pretty does not appear to be the correct word to employ. Nor does beautiful answer, either. Those words do not go far enough. Oh, it was marvelous—marvelous. It is the initial thing I have ever witnessed that imagination could not make better. It simply satisfied me in this spot”—she placed a hand upon her breast—“it produced a strange, peculiar pain and still it was an agreeable pain. Have you ever experienced a pain of that sort, Mr. Abernethy?”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0051 }

“Well now, I simply am unable to recall that I ever did.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0052 }

“I experience it frequently—each time I behold something magnificent. However, they ought not to name that exquisite spot the Avenue. Such a title lacks any significance. They ought to name it—let me think—the Petal Road of Delight. Does that not sound like a delightful, creative name? Whenever a location or an individual has a name I dislike, I invariably invent a different one and constantly refer to them that way in my mind. A girl resided at the orphanage whose name was Hepzibah Jenkins, yet I constantly pictured her as Rosalia DeVere. Others might refer to that spot as the Avenue, but I will perpetually refer to it as the Petal Road of Delight. Is there truly merely one more mile remaining before we arrive at home? I am happy and I am sad. I am sad since this ride has proved so enjoyable, and I am perpetually sad whenever enjoyable experiences conclude. An even more enjoyable event might follow, yet a person can never know for certain. And frequently it happens that it is not more enjoyable. At least, that has proven true in my life. However, I am happy contemplating arriving at home. As you know, I have not possessed an actual home for as far back as I can recall. Just contemplating arriving at a genuine, proper home causes that enjoyable pain to return to me. Oh, is that not lovely!”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0053 }

Having crested the hill, they were driving along when a pond appeared below them, its long, winding shape making it seem nearly like a river. It was crossed in the middle by a bridge, and extending from that point down to its bottom extremity, where a band of amber-colored sand-hills enclosed it against the dark blue gulf outside, the water displayed a magnificent display of constantly changing colors—the delicate shades of saffron, pink, and airy green, alongside other subtle hues that remain unnamed to this day. Upstream from the bridge, the pond extended into bordering thickets of fir and maple, resting fully dark and see-through beneath their trembling shadows. In various spots, a wild plum tilted out over the shore like a girl dressed in white stepping carefully toward her image in the water. The clear, sadly sweet singing of frogs floated up from the marsh located at the top of the pond. Sitting on a hillside further off, a small gray house peeked from behind a white apple orchard, and a light glowed out from one of its windows, even though full darkness had not yet fallen.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0054 }

“That’s Pembroke’s pond,” Obed said.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0055 }

“Oh, that name is not to my liking, either. I will name it—let me think—the Lake of Glassy Waters. Yes, that name fits it properly. The thrill tells me so. I experience a thrill whenever I discover a name that fits perfectly. Do you ever get a thrill from things?”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0056 }

Obed pondered.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0057 }

“Well now, yes. Seeing those ugly white grubs that the spade turns up in the cucumber beds always gives me a sort of thrill. I hate how they look.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0058 }

“Oh, I feel that cannot be precisely that sort of excitement. Is it possible for it to be? There appears to be little link between larvae and pools of gleaming waters, doesn't there? However, why is it referred to as Pembroke’s pond by other folks?”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0059 }

“I guess it is due to Mr. Pembroke residing up in that dwelling. Pear Hill is what his property is called. Were it not for the large shrub behind it, Grey Shutters would be visible from this spot. However, we are required to cross the bridge and take the route along the road, which makes it almost a half-mile longer.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0060 }

“Are there any young daughters belonging to Mr. Pembroke? Though not particularly small—roughly as big as I am.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0061 }

“A child around eleven belongs to him. Isolde is her name.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0062 }

“Oh!” she gasped, taking a deep breath. “That name is absolutely wonderful!”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0063 }

“Well now, I am not sure. It strikes me that there is something terribly pagan about it. I would prefer Odette or Mary or a similarly practical name. However, a schoolmaster was lodging there at the time Isolde was born, so they let him choose her name, and Isolde was what he called her.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0064 }

“In that case, I wish a schoolmaster such as him had been present when I came into the world. Ah, this is the bridge right here. My eyes are going to be squeezed shut. Crossing bridges always fills me with dread. I am unable to stop picturing that the structures might collapse together like a pocketknife and catch us right as we reach the midpoint. For that reason, my eyes stay closed. Even so, I am compelled to unclose them every time once I sense the center is approaching. You see, should the bridge actually collapse, my desire would be to witness the collapsing. The rumble it produces is so pleasant! The rumbling aspect is something I constantly enjoy. Is it not wonderful that the world contains such a multitude of pleasant things? Well, our crossing is complete. At this point, I shall glance behind us. Good night, beloved Lake of Glassy Waters. My habit is to bid good night to objects of my affection, exactly like I do with human beings. My feeling is that it pleases them. The water appears to be beaming back at me.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0065 }

After they had proceeded up the next incline and rounded a bend, Obed remarked:
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0066 }

“We are quite close to home at this point. That is Grey Shutters over—”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0067 }

“Oh, don’t tell me,” she cut in out of breath, clutching his arm which was partially lifted and closing her eyes so as not to witness his motion. “Let me guess. I’m sure I’ll guess right.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0068 }

Opening her eyes, she surveyed her surroundings. The top of a hill was where they were situated. Although the sun had gone down a while ago, the terrain remained distinct in the soft glow of dusk. Out to the west, a deep-colored church spire mounted up opposite a sky the color of a marigold. A small valley lay beneath, and past it stretched a lengthy, softly ascending incline upon which cozy farmsteads were dispersed. Eagerly and longingly, the child's gaze jumped from one place to the next. Eventually, her sight rested upon a single homestead off to the left, set deep behind the road, faintly gleaming white owing to flowering trees within the dimness of the encircling forest. Above this spot, set in the pure southwestern sky, a large, clear-white star burned bright, resembling a beacon offering direction and hope.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0069 }

“Is that not it?” she asked, making a pointing gesture.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0070 }

With great pleasure, Obed struck the sorrel's back using the reins.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0071 }

“Indeed, you’ve hit upon it! However, I suppose Mrs. Tranter gave a description of it so you’d recognize it.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0072 }

“No, she didn’t—really she didn’t. Every single thing she said could easily have applied to almost any of those other places. I did not possess any true concept of its appearance. However, the moment my eyes fell upon it, a sensation that it was home came over me. Oh, I feel just as though I am living in a dream. Are you aware that my arm is likely bruised from my elbow upwards, because I have pinched myself time and again today. Every now and then, a dreadful, nauseating sensation would overwhelm me, making me terribly frightened that everything was merely a dream. After that, I would give myself a pinch to test if it were genuine—until all at once it occurred to me that even if it were nothing more than a dream, continuing to dream as long as possible was the better choice; therefore, I ceased pinching. Yet it is genuine, and our arrival at home is close.”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0073 }

Releasing a joyful sigh, she became quiet once more. Obed shifted uncomfortably. He was pleased that Thirza, rather than himself, was tasked with informing this homeless child that she would not be receiving the home she so desired. Their drive took them across Sowerby’s Hollow, where night had already settled, though it remained light enough for Mrs. Agatha to observe them from her position at the window, and they continued up the slope and into the extended driveway of Grey Shutters. Upon reaching the dwelling, Obed was pulling back from the impending disclosure with a intensity that bewildered him. His thoughts were not centered on Thirza, himself, or the hardship this error would likely inflict on them, but rather on how crushed the girl would be. Contemplating the extinction of that ecstatic glow in her eyes gave him a distressing sensation that he was about to participate in a killing—a sentiment very similar to what he experienced whenever he was forced to slaughter a lamb, calf, or any other harmless small animal.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0074 }

The poplars' leaves made a silky rustling noise all around the yard, which was rather dark when they turned inside.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0075 }

“Hear the trees speaking while they sleep,” she murmured, while he set her down upon the earth. “They must be having such lovely dreams!”
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0076 }

Next, gripping the carpet-bag that held “all her worldly goods” firmly, she went after him inside the residence.
{: #nw-v01-c02-p0077 }
